0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Muscadet is not a single AOC but a family. The four appellations each have a different geographic extent and soil character, of which Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine is by far the most important, making up 85% of the family's output. In addition, sur lie ageing on the lees and the "communal cru" classification system have lifted Muscadet from an inexpensive aperitif to a white wine worth cellaring.

Learning Objectives

🗺️ Compare the four Muscadet AOCs

Understand how Muscadet, MSM, MCDGL and MCDLL differ in geography, soil and style

🦠 Master sur lie ageing

Understand how ageing on the lees (at least until March of the following year) adds complexity, body and a prickle of fizz to Muscadet

🏆 Know the Crus Communaux classification

Clisson, Gorges, Le Pallet — the soils and style differences of the three flagship crus

🦪 Understand Muscadet tasting and food pairing

Why Muscadet sur lie is the best choice with oysters, mussels and seafood

2.title: 🗺️ Comparing the Four Muscadet AOCs
2.highlights.0.title: Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine (MSM)
2.highlights.0.content: The most important! 85% of the family's output, where the Sèvre and Maine rivers meet; diverse granite + schist + gabbro soils, the richest minerality
2.highlights.1.title: Muscadet-Côtes-de-Grandlieu (MCDGL)
2.highlights.1.content: Around Lac de Grand-Lieu, mainly clay + sandstone; a rounder, softer style that is very approachable
2.content:
Although the four Muscadet AOCs share the same variety (Melon de Bourgogne), their locations and soils differ, and each has its own style:

🥇 Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine 85%
Granite · Schist · Gabbro
Most refined minerality, strongest ageing potential
🏞️ Muscadet-Côtes-de-Grandlieu Minor
Clay · Sandstone
Round and soft, plenty of fruit, easy-drinking
🌿 Muscadet-Coteaux-de-la-Loire Rare
Schist · Volcanic rock
Lightest and crispest, lively high acidity
🍾 Muscadet (basic) Simple
No specific geographic limits
Everyday drinking, fresh and simple
2.quiz.question: Roughly what share of the whole Muscadet family's output does Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine (MSM) account for?
2.quiz.explanation: Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine is the most important AOC in the Muscadet family, accounting for about 85% of total output. It lies where the Sèvre and Maine rivers meet, with diverse granite, schist and gabbro soils, and is also the core region of the Crus Communaux classification.
3.title: 🦠 Sur Lie: Three Levels of Lees Ageing
3.highlights.0.title: Underground concrete tanks: a Nantes speciality
3.highlights.0.content: All Muscadet sur lie ageing takes place in "underground concrete tanks" (underground vats lined with glass or ceramic tiles), a traditional facility unique to the Nantes region; the stable underground temperature is key to ageing quality
3.highlights.1.title: Three ageing levels, three style levels
3.highlights.1.content: Short (< 6 months) → fresh and lively; medium (< 18 months) → rich structure; long (> 24 months) → complex ageing, corresponding to the 10 Crus Communaux classification
3.content:
Sur lie (ageing on the lees) is the core craft of Muscadet. It is mandatory in all three regional AOCs (MSM, MCDGL, MCDLL), and the 10 Crus Communaux require much longer ageing (a minimum of about 17–18 months, most 24 months or more) — the length of time decides the level of style

🏗️ Traditional storage: underground concrete tanks (underground vats lined with glass or ceramic tiles) — a traditional facility unique to Nantes, where the stable underground temperature ensures slow, even contact with the lees.

💧 Short sur lie < 6 months
Basic Muscadet AOC
Fresh and lively, clear floral-fruit notes, light with high acidity, ideal for drinking young
🌿 Medium sur lie < 18 months
Regional AOCs (MSM / MCDGL / MCDLL)
Rich structure, bread and butter notes, CO₂ prickle, balanced complexity
🏆 Long sur lie ≥ 17–18 months (most > 24)
The 10 Crus Communaux
Complex ageing, honey and quince, spice and minerals, cellarable for 10–40 years
After harvest
🍇 Alcoholic fermentation finishes

The dead yeast (lees) settles naturally at the bottom of the underground concrete tank; the wine is not racked or filtered, and the long process of autolysis begins.

Autolysis
🦠 Yeast cells break down and release complexity

The yeast cell walls break down, releasing amino acids, polysaccharides and glycerol, which give bread and butter notes and a rich mouthfeel; a trace of CO₂ is also retained, giving a lively prickle and protecting against oxidation.

March of the following year
📋 Minimum legal period for regional AOCs

The three regional AOCs (MSM, MCDGL, MCDLL) all require ageing on the lees until at least 1 March of the following year. This is the legal threshold for the "Muscadet Sur Lie" label.

24–48 months
🏆 Crus Communaux: the longest ageing

All 10 classified crus require long sur lie ageing (a minimum of about 17–18 months, most 24 months or more); Château-Thébaud can reach up to 48 months, and top vintages show 10–40 years of ageing potential.
3.quiz.question: According to the official rules, which Muscadet AOCs make sur lie ageing mandatory?
3.quiz.options.1: The three regional AOCs: MSM, MCDGL and MCDLL
3.quiz.explanation: Under the official rules, the three regional AOCs — Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine (MSM), Muscadet-Côtes-de-Grandlieu (MCDGL) and Muscadet-Coteaux-de-la-Loire (MCDLL) — all require sur lie ageing, until at least 1 March of the following year. The 10 Crus Communaux require much longer ageing (a minimum of about 17–18 months, most 24 months or more). The basic generic Muscadet AOC may choose whether to state sur lie.
4.title: 🏆 Crus Communaux: 10 Officially Recognised Crus
4.highlights.0.title: Clisson — Power ★★★
4.highlights.0.content: Granite bedrock, 24–36 months sur lie, high alcohol, full and round, with aromas of ripe pear, peach, ripe citrus, honey and quince; the flagship cru of southern MSM
4.highlights.1.title: Gorges — Length ★★★
4.highlights.1.content: Gabbro subsoil, the oldest cru, 24–40 months sur lie, closed when young, with mint, lemon, smoke and flint aromas and the strongest mineral tension
4.content:
The Crus Communaux, established in 2011, are a milestone in Muscadet's quality revolution. Nine lie in MSM, and Champtoceaux is the only one in MCDLL. Each cru has an officially recognised keyword for its character:

💪 Clisson ★★★ Power · granite
Sur lie 24–36 months · southern MSM
High alcohol and full, ripe pear · honey · quince, the highest ageing complexity
〰️ Gorges ★★★ Length · gabbro
Sur lie 24–40 months · Sèvre hills
Closed when young, mint · smoke · flint, the longest mineral tension
🪨 Le Pallet ★★★ Unctuosity · gneiss
Sur lie 18+ months · centre of the Sèvre right bank
Rich and smooth, fruit · minerals, silky texture
⚖️ Goulaine ★★ Balance · gneiss + mica schist
Sur lie 20–30 months · marshland hills
Harvested first, ripe fruit · honey, balanced and elegant
🏰 Château-Thébaud ★★ Refinement · granodiorite
Sur lie 36–48 months · Maine hills
Aniseed · liquorice · spice, elegant saline finish
🔬 Mouzillon-Tillières ★★ Complexity · composite metamorphic rocks
Sur lie 24+ months · MSM
Diverse soils give complex mineral layering
💪🏼 Monnières-Saint Fiacre ★ Body · gneiss
Sur lie 24+ months · Sèvre left bank
Plump and smooth, orange blossom · exotic fruit · beeswax
🌸 La Haye Fouassière ★ Elegance · orthogneiss
Sur lie 18 months (the shortest) · westernmost cru
Mint · floral · flint minerality, early-maturing and elegant
✨ Vallet ★ Opulence · mica schist
Sur lie 18+ months · inland northeast MSM
Abundant floral-fruit notes, regular late ripening, elegant and luxurious
🥂 Champtoceaux ★ Silkiness · mica schist + amphibolite
Sur lie 17+ months · the only one in MCDLL
Silky and smooth, orange blossom · citrus · spice, vanilla with age
🔑 Exam focus: Clisson (granite → Power), Gorges (gabbro → Length) and Le Pallet (gneiss → Unctuosity) are the three flagships; Château-Thébaud has the longest ageing (36–48 months); Champtoceaux is the only cru outside MSM.
4.quiz.question: Which Cru Communal is the only one NOT located in Muscadet-Sèvre-et-Maine (MSM)?
4.quiz.explanation: Champtoceaux is the only one of the 10 Crus Communaux in Muscadet-Coteaux-de-la-Loire (MCDLL), on the hills on both banks of the Loire near Ancenis. Its soils are mainly composite metamorphic rocks such as mica schist, gneiss and amphibolite, its style is officially defined as "Silkiness", and it requires at least 17 months sur lie. The other nine crus all lie within MSM.
